properties.chose:
ACCEPTED on @ajs's word, 2026-09-30, in the dev_reflow2 hub session: "Go with your recommendations". The recommendation was option (b), Alex's ask as Anthony clarified it: "each tier is its own reflow2 graph that others are linked to vertically". Each tier is its own design, intent flows down to the tiers below, evidence rolls up to the tiers above, and what a tier holds is already settled by req:a-design-over-the-parts-of-one-thing-holds-what-no-part-owns.
The LINKING MECHANISM is NOT settled. That covers what crosses the boundary and how: export_surface carries no Verifications today, and nothing crosses a design boundary. It is designed when the first real tiered design needs it, not ahead of one. Candidates already in hand are the flo2 and dev_reflow2 hubs, and the knowledge-graph hub over graph-primitives and the ideal knowledge graph.
Options (a), one graph with levels, and (c), a rendering only, stay on the record as roads not taken.
properties.decision:
🕐 DEFERRED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY — THE SHAPE ONLY, AND DEFERRED IS NOT DECLINED. Asked which form vertical linking should take, he chose to **fix `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent` FIRST and decide the shape after**: every option below makes decomposition more load-bearing, the coverage hole is already measured with a field instance, and settling a tier shape on top of a broken roll-up would bake the defect into precisely the boundary where nobody can see it.

⭐ **AND THE ASK IS NARROWER THAN "OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN" SUGGESTS — ANTHONY CLARIFIED WHAT ALEX MEANS:** *"I think my brother is more indicating that each tier is its own reflow2 graph that others are linked to vertically."* ⇒ **ALEX IS ASKING FOR OPTION (b): A GRAPH PER TIER, WITH VERTICAL LINKS BETWEEN THEM.** Not one graph with levels, and not a rendering. When this re-opens, (b) is the stated starting position rather than an open field — the others stay on the record as roads, not as equals.

⇒ WHAT IS SETTLED: nothing about the shape.
⇒ WHAT IS NOW LIVE WORK: `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent` (moved to **accepted** on his word) → `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` (planned, `cmp:detect`). ⚠️ Its gap acknowledgement `decision:ack:1947285897ace4dc` — *"deferred on Anthony's word 2026-07-28… a handshake to design rather than a check to write"* — was WITHDRAWN, since a parked gap and a planned capability cannot both describe the same work.

🎯 **RE-ASK TRIGGER, NAMED SO THIS CANNOT DEGRADE INTO NEVER ASKED AGAIN** (the shape `dec:the-other-uaf-domains-wait-for-a-project-that-needs-them` set): re-open when the coverage check is BUILT and one of — (i) a real design is split across an authority boundary and someone needs a parent's number to mean something, (ii) `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` is settled, since binding-versus-visible is this question in disguise, or (iii) a second user asks for tiers.
⚠️ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DEFERRAL WRONG: someone building a tier hierarchy in prose or file layout while waiting — the workaround that looks like patience and costs exactly what the deferral was meant to avoid.
📌 NOT ANSWERED BY THE RENDERING ROUTE: `dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect` covers what a reader is SHOWN. It composes with this and does not substitute for it — a first version of that node claimed otherwise and was corrected.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`) 2026-08-14, sharpened by Anthony's framing.

ALEX'S WORDS: *"I found myself wanting a top level graph and then graphs for the different components. The top level graph could hold information about the project as a whole and be aware of the graphs for the subcomponents of the graph (UI, API, e2e tests, etc.). In those graphs, we can put the fine details of those components, such as storing information about how migrations are performed in the database. The top level graph could contain domain knowledge that is relevant to all the graphs. This is the system of systems concept."*

ANTHONY'S FRAMING: *"instead of being peer-to-peer, this is more tier-to-tier. If peer-to-peer linking is 'horizontal', this idea is more 'vertical' between tiers… you could have a 'leadership' level that doesn't need to know every detail… a 'management' layer that knows more… a 'worker' graph that knows details. At each layer, it is probably the exchange of breadth for depth. In the military, we had 'strategic', 'operational', and 'tactical'."*

═══ ⭐⭐ WHY VERTICAL IS NOT HORIZONTAL REUSED ═══

**HORIZONTAL is an INTERFACE.** Two designs meet at a contract; neither contains the other; the coordinate is *"I designed against your published surface at this hash"* (`cap:mirror-surface`). A mirror is a REFERENCE.
**VERTICAL is a DECOMPOSITION.** The upper tier holds intent, the lower tier holds requirements decomposed FROM it, and delivery ROLLS UP — a containment-and-satisfaction relation with arithmetic attached.

⇒ **reflow2 HAS decomposition INSIDE a graph and mirroring ACROSS graphs. It does not have decomposition ACROSS graphs.** That is the gap, and the existing federation work does not close it.

═══ 🛑 MEASURED CORRECTION TO THE RECORD — the parent direction is NOT built ═══

`dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` asserts *"THE MECHANISM FOR THE PARENT DIRECTION ALREADY EXISTS… ANTICIPATED and BUILT, not missing."* **Too strong:**
  1. `report.rs` rolls delivery up via `decomposed_children` = `self.incoming(parent_id, DECOMPOSES)` (`graph.rs:1143`).
  2. Reads are scoped to the bound `graph_id` and `create_edge` resolves BOTH endpoints in scope — a `DECOMPOSES` edge between two graphs cannot be created at all.
  3. ⇒ **Nothing rolls up across a design boundary.** `cap:derived-completion` is verified WITHIN one graph.
  4. Mirroring does not rescue it: `export_surface` publishes published Interfaces, the artifacts that SPECIFY/REALIZE them, published Requirements and the Project — **no Verifications.** Delivery = satisfied AND realized AND PASSING CHECK, so **the evidence is exactly the part that does not cross.**
📌 That node warns *"READ THE EXPORT, NOT THE SUMMARY"* after making this error once, then makes it again a paragraph later about a different mechanism.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE TIER FRAMING TURNS A KNOWN DEFECT INTO A WORSE ONE ═══

`req:decomposition-covers-its-parent`: reflow2 rolls delivery UP and **never checks that children COVER the parent** — a parent split into two children addressing a tenth reports DELIVERED once both close. Measured instance: reflow's monolith split into 01a–01f, `context_management` and `self_improvement` present in all six originals, absent from all seven children, **unnoticed for months**.

🛑 **"EXCHANGE OF BREADTH FOR DEPTH" IS THE MECHANISM THAT HIDES IT.** A decomposition by SUBJECT drops what belongs to no single subject; trading breadth for depth is that drop made deliberately, tier after tier. Inside one graph a reader sees both sides. **Across an authority boundary they cannot: the strategic tier sees `delivered` and is structurally unable to see what fell between the children** — and it is the tier least likely to look.

═══ 📌 WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS ═══

  · `dec:nested-graphs` (ACCEPTED 2026-07-25) — a graph per OWNERSHIP boundary, `level`s inside; *a graph per system* rejected as a RULE because every seam costs a coordinate, a roll-up and a freshness check. **Alex's UI/API/e2e split is depth under one owner, so under today's rule it is ONE graph — which is exactly the rule his ask strains.**
  · **THE LEADERSHIP TIER IS ALREADY THERE, EXPRESSED HORIZONTALLY** — that decision calls `docs/org-scale-vision.md`'s *"one graph the whole company plans in"* a road not taken and replaces it with *"the CEO's objectives are one design that others MIRROR."* Anthony's point is that a mirror may be the wrong shape, and the roll-up finding says he is right: mirroring gives visibility, not arithmetic.
  · `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` — requirements already cross; the **Decision** cannot. Its unanswered question is this one in disguise: **is a mirrored Decision BINDING on the far side, or only VISIBLE?** Binding is what a tier means; visible is what a peer means.
  · `dec:idea-many-graphs-one-store`, `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` — both open, both the ownership rule strained by people with depth and no authority boundary.

🛑 MODELLING TRAP TO NAME BEFORE ANYONE BUILDS: `Component.level` (component → subsystem → system → system_of_systems → enterprise) is an **ASSEMBLY** ladder — *part of*. Strategic/operational/tactical is an **AUTHORITY and ABSTRACTION** ladder — a tactical design is not PART OF a strategic one, it REALIZES it. Reusing `level` conflates two relations, and `hierarchy_issues` already reads it the assembly way.

📌 UAF, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `dec:the-other-uaf-domains-wait-for-a-project-that-needs-them` names its re-ask trigger for the four DOMAINS (information, materiel, personnel, states), not for layering. **This note does not trigger it.**

OPTIONS — SHAPE DEFERRED, and (b) is what Alex is asking for.
(a) ANSWER WITH THE ACCEPTED RULE — one graph, `level`s, `cap:scoped-analysis`. Correct today; occurred to neither user.
(b) ⭐ **ALEX'S ASK** — VERTICAL AS A FIRST-CLASS RELATION: a graph per tier, cross-graph decomposition, intent down and EVIDENCE up. Cost: cross-graph edges, or a mirror carrying verification state; reopens `create_edge`'s endpoint invariant, which is deliberate and well-argued.
(c) VERTICAL AS MIRRORING, AS TODAY. Cheapest, already decided; the parent can compute nothing about its children.
(d) TIERS INSIDE ONE GRAPH — an abstraction ladder distinct from `Component.level`, tiers as a projection. No separate ownership or write locks, which is most of what a tier split is for.
(e) ⭐ **CHOSEN AS SEQUENCING, NOT AS SHAPE** — fix the coverage check first.

📌 ALEX'S OWN EXAMPLE IS STILL UNHOUSED: *"how migrations are performed in the database"* is not a requirement, capability or interface — operational know-how attached to a component, with nowhere to go today but an Artifact or a requirement's prose.

═══ 🔓 RE-OPENED 2026-09-26 ON ANTHONY'S WORD ("Re-open Alex's tiers") ═══
The re-ask trigger this deferral named is met (fact:the-tier-deferral-is-due-to-be-re-asked-2026-09-26): the coverage check it waited behind reads realized, and a second user asked for tiers on 2026-09-22. Anthony asked again the same day as this re-opening, as systems-of-systems tiers (component designs → an engine hub → a car hub → a hub over car types), and kept as intent that a design over the parts of one thing holds what no part owns (req:a-design-over-the-parts-of-one-thing-holds-what-no-part-owns). That settles what a tier HOLDS. What this node asks, and what is now open again, is how tiers LINK: option (b), a graph per tier with intent flowing down and evidence rolling up across the boundary, remains the stated starting position. The cost named above still stands: nothing crosses a design boundary today, and export_surface carries no Verifications. Status moved from deferred to proposed; the deferral above is kept as the record of why it waited.

properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill, sharpened by Anthony's vertical/horizontal framing, deferred as to shape on his word, and then narrowed again when he clarified that Alex means a graph per tier rather than levels or a view. That clarification is recorded on the options list itself rather than only in prose, because the re-ask trigger will bring someone back to this node months from now and "options, none chosen" would hand them a blank field when the user has in fact stated one. The re-ask trigger follows the precedent `dec:the-other-uaf-domains-wait-for-a-project-that-needs-them` set, including naming what would make the deferral wrong. The measured correction to `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` lives here rather than being edited into that node, because withdrawing another node's claim deserves its own visibility rather than a quiet overwrite.
